content: Bread dough rises because yeast consumes sugars and releases carbon dioxide gas, creating bubbles that expand the dough. Bakers let it rest to allow this fermentation process to fully develop, which strengthens the gluten network and improves flavor. This resting period ensures the bread has a light, airy texture and a well-structured crumb once it is finally baked in the oven.
